1→# Subdivision & Development Engineering Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Drainage analysis, stormwater detention and water quality controls, grading, retaining walls, easements, storm drain design, subdivision platting, standard details, and construction inspection for City of Austin and Austin ETJ projects. Bridges with `wwp` (water/wastewater), `fwp` (floodplain & creek buffers), `ta` (transportation/ROW), and `el` (environmental — CEFs, EARZ, watershed classification).
     6→
     7→SDE is the largest discipline by code volume; expect to coordinate findings across most of the other disciplines.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Watershed Protection Department; governs drainage design, easements, ponds, RSMP
    12→- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — water quality controls (SCMs/GSI), grading, IWM, CEFs, EARZ liners
    13→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Title 25** — chapters 25-7 (drainage), 25-8 (environmental/water quality), 25-4/30-2 (subdivision)
    14→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) §13.2** — retaining wall structural and ROW requirements
    15→- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM) §2.5** — construction plan content, PE seal, sheet standards
    16→- **City of Austin Standard Specifications & Standard Drawings (SSM/Std Specs)** — 508S outlet structures, 661 series WQ details, 594S gabions, 414S waterstops, 623S dry-stack rock, 658S void mitigation
    17→- **RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24, effective July 15, 2024)** — Regional Stormwater Management Program
    18→- **General Site Plan Notes for COA** and **Environmental Review Requirements** — cover sheet and plan note templates
    19→
    20→Atlas 14 rainfall is mandatory for submittals on/after Nov 25, 2019 (DCM 2.3.0). Approved drainage modeling software: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, PondPack, StormCAD, CivilStorm (DCM 1.2.5).
    21→
    22→## Regulatory pathway
    23→
    24→| Action | Path | Typical timeline |
    25→|---|---|---|
    26→| Concept/feasibility review | Optional Pre-Development Consultation; RSMP Feasibility Meeting if pursuing RSMP | 4–8 weeks |
    27→| Subdivision | Preliminary Plan → Subdivision Construction Plans → Final Plat | 6–18 months |
    28→| Site Plan (commercial / multifamily) | SDP application → Completeness Check → Update Cycles → Approval | 9–18 months in current cycle times |
    29→| RSMP participation | Feasibility Meeting **before** Completeness Check → Application Package → Approval Letter → Agreement → Payment | 3–6 months to Approval Letter; payment before permit issuance |
    30→| Construction permit | Site Development Permit issued after plan approval; pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282) | 2–6 weeks post-approval |
    31→| Inspection / acceptance | DSD/WPD inspection through construction; engineer certifications before CO; SCM acceptance for SF/duplex (City takes maintenance); restrictive covenant for commercial/MF (owner maintains) | continuous |
    32→
    33→Key sequencing trap: **RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before formal Completeness Check.** If RSMP is in play, schedule that meeting at the start of design.
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→### Drainage performance standard (DCM 1.2.2.D)
    38→
    39→- **No-increase rule** at every point of discharge for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms. Existing and proposed conditions modeled separately.
    40→- **Exception:** direct discharge into Lady Bird Lake, Lake Austin, Lake Travis, the Colorado River, or qualifying Waller Creek TIRZ properties (DCM 1.2.2.F).
    41→- **Atlas 14 rainfall** for all submittals after Nov 25, 2019. Pre-Atlas 14 phased developments may use DCM 1.2.2.H hybrid criteria.
    42→- Off-site contributing areas modeled at **existing IC** for pond performance (DCM 8.3.2.A) but **fully developed** for spillway/embankment design (DCM 8.3.3.A). Both apply to the same pond.
    43→
    44→### Water quality controls (LDC § 25-8-211; ECM 1.6)
    45→
    46→- **Trigger:** any new + redeveloped IC > 8,000 SF outside BSZ; **all** development in the Barton Springs Zone (no threshold).
    47→- **Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) mandatory** since Nov 7, 2022 (LDC § 25-8-213(C)). Conventional sed/filtration ponds and wet ponds require a documented exemption: highly contaminated runoff land use, off-site treatment ≥ 10 acres of currently untreated developed area, or site IC > 90% gross area (LDC § 25-8-213(D)).
    48→- **WQV formula** (ECM 1.6.2.A): WQV = (0.5 in + 0.1 in per 10% IC over 20%) × DA (ac) × 3,630. Drawdown within 48 hours. Applies to all IC on site, not just new IC.
    49→- **EARZ controls (LDC § 25-8-213(A)(2); ECM 1.6.2.C):** impermeable liner required — geomembrane (≥ 30 mils, UV resistant) or concrete (basins < 1,000 SF). Clay liners (Std Detail 661-2) **prohibited** over EARZ regardless of permeability testing. Vegetative filter strips are the only exemption.
    50→- **Rain garden cap:** 2 acres contributing drainage area (ECM 1.6.7.H). Larger = biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C). Recommended max 50 acres per WQ control (ECM 1.6.2.A).
    51→- **Wet pond minimum permanent pool:** > 0.5 ac (21,780 SF) (ECM 1.6.6.A.1).
    52→- **IWM (Innovative Water Management):** commercial sites with required landscape area must irrigate ≥ 50% with stormwater or leave undisturbed (LDC § 25-2-1008; ECM 2.4.9). 1:2 minimum drainage-to-landscape ratio.
    53→
    54→### Stormwater detention
    55→
    56→- **2-year on-site control required regardless of RSMP** (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8).
    57→- **Detention drawdown:** max 24 hr for flood detention (DCM 8.3.2.C).
    58→- **Regional pond threshold:** > 64 ac contributing drainage area triggers WPD project-by-project review and geotechnical-based slope design (DCM 8.3.2.B; DCM 8.3.3.F).
    59→- **Dam classification:** SWM pond embankment ≥ 6 ft at any point along the perimeter → dam (DCM 8.3.3.B.1). Triggers PMF design, 20-ft clear zone (no trees/woody vegetation upstream and downstream of toe), and TCEQ jurisdiction concerns.
    60→- **Storm drain connection** required when within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system (DCM 1.2.3.C, as amended 9-8-2025). RSMP does **not** waive this.
    61→
    62→### Grading and slopes
    63→
    64→- General cut/fill side slopes: max 3H:1V (DCM 8.3.3.F; DCM 6.4.1.D). Rock slopes steeper than 3:1 require geotechnical stability report.
    65→- Wet pond earthen slopes max 3:1 (ECM 1.6.6.C.6); vegetated bench between 3:1 and 4:1 (or 4:1–5:1 for ponds ≥ 2 ac, ECM Table 1-9B).
    66→- WQ facility maintenance drives: ≤ 15% longitudinal, ≤ 5% transverse (DCM 1.2.4.E.1.e).
    67→- Temporary ESC slopes 2:1 or flatter (ECM 1.4.5). Final slopes > 15% require erosion control matting at toe and top.
    68→- Elevations must be NAVD88 (or equivalent absolute datum), not site-relative. BCM 4.4.3.1 requires a permanent benchmark on the plot plan.
    69→
    70→### Retaining walls (TCM § 13.2)
    71→
    72→- **< 2 ft (minor structure):** no PE, no geotech, no separate building permit. Construction waiver available unless wall supports roadway embankment.
    73→- **≥ 2 ft:** licensed PE design + geotechnical investigation required.
    74→- **≥ 4 ft:** structural plan submittal + calculations before site plan approval + separate **building permit** (IBC). Cover sheet note required.
    75→- **> 10 ft and supporting roadway embankment:** 20-ft truck-accessible maintenance zone at base (TCM 13.2.9).
    76→- **In/adjacent to ROW:** D1 ≤ H1 rule triggers full §13.2 review. 5-ft minimum face-to-back-of-curb. External components (geogrid, soldier piles) need ≥ 36 in cover. Private walls **not allowed in ROW** without encroachment agreement (City Council approval).
    77→- **Drainage easement walls:** not categorically prohibited — Director approval + license/encroachment agreement + utility encasement.
    78→- **Inside SCMs:** dry-stacked rock prohibited (ECM 1.6.3.B.7). Grouted rock walls inside SCMs require impermeable barrier. Waterstops required at expansion joints (ECM 1.6.3.B.6; Std Spec 414S.4.E).
    79→- **Safety rails:** not a universal "> 4 ft" trigger. Triggered when wall supports roadway embankment adjacent to sidewalk/roadway, OR when wall is adjacent to park/playground/SF/MF residential with backslope toward wall (TCM 13.2.10).
    80→
    81→### Easements (LDC § 25-7-151, -152; DCM 1.2.4)
    82→
    83→- Open drainage easement: min 25 ft (DCM 1.2.4.G.1).
    84→- Enclosed system: per pipe-diameter/invert-depth table — min 20 ft for shallowest/smallest pipes; up to 40 ft for large-diameter deep inverts. **No 15-ft minimum in current DCM.** Half-width allowed outside ROW when parallel to ROW (Note 2).
    85→- Easement extends to the **larger of** the COA fully-developed 100-yr WSE or DCM minimum widths (DCM 1.2.4.F). COA floodplain typically broader than FEMA.
    86→- COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain delineation required when contributing DA ≥ 64 ac (DCM 1.2.6.A.1).
    87→- **Document types** (City administrative practice): Public Drainage Easement; Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance (private maintenance); Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance and Permitted Obstructions (combined flows or authorized structures).
    88→- **Water Quality Easement** required for irrigation/infiltration fields of retention/irrigation SCMs (ECM 1.6.7.A.4.c) — distinct from drainage easement.
    89→- **Shared infrastructure** (DCM 1.2.4.E.3): Restrictive Covenant, UDA, or Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance when serving multiple lots. UDA must be City Legal–approved and recorded before site plan approval.
    90→- **Dam clear zone:** 20-ft tree-free zone within dedicated easement for dam-classified ponds (DCM 8.3.3.B.5).
    91→- Buildings and parking **may not encroach** on the 25- or 100-yr floodplain (LDC § 25-7-92).
    92→
    93→### RSMP — Regional Stormwater Management Program (DCM 8.2)
    94→
    95→- Alternative to **on-site detention only.** Does not waive: 2-yr on-site control, storm drain connection, WQ SCMs, existing storm drain condition verification (DCM 5.3.6), or any other code.
    96→- **Three pathways:**
    97→  - **DCM 1.2.2.G (Simplified):** commercial/MF/mixed-use ≤ 0.5 ac, **or** SF subdivision ≤ 1 ac (no preliminary plan). All four criteria all-or-nothing.
    98→  - **DCM 8.2.2 (General):** larger sites in participating watersheds within COA full-purpose. Requires three-scenario HEC-HMS model (existing; proposed w/ conceptual pond; proposed w/o detention), downstream capacity demonstration for fully developed 100-yr, drainage easement for unconditional 100-yr conveyance.
    99→  - **Prior RSMP Participation:** redevelopment under existing executed RSMP Agreement bound to the land; case-by-case O-Type Approval Letter.
   100→- **Order of preference** (DCM 8.2.2.B): (1) improvement of downstream system/SCMs, (2) off-site detention, (3) easement dedication/land donation, (4) payment in lieu. Payment selection must be justified or RSMP Team must accept the departure.
   101→- **Categorically unavailable:** subdivisions in the Travis County ETJ. For non-subdivision ETJ projects, a Travis County Detention Waiver is required first.
   102→- **Watershed eligibility** confirmed via RSMP Feasibility Viewer or Austin Watersheds List — not determinable from plan sheets alone.
   103→- **Payment rate** updated annually on October 1 (ENR-CCI indexed). Current calculation at austintexas.gov/RSMP.
   104→- **SMART Housing discount:** 10–50% RSMP payment discount for 10–50% SMART Housing units maintained ≥ 40 yr (requires SMART Housing Certification Letter).
   105→- Special coordination: **PARD** acceptance if discharging onto/through parkland (Chapter 26 process if charter-protected); **TxDOT District Engineer** letter if discharging onto/across TxDOT ROW or connecting to TxDOT storm drains; **downstream jurisdiction** approval if watershed drains out of Austin's jurisdiction.
   106→
   107→### Interbasin diversion (LDC § 25-8-365)
   108→
   109→- Minor diversion threshold: < 20% of gross site area **AND** < 1 ac (both must be met).
   110→- ≥ 20% **or** ≥ 1 ac → Administrative Environmental Variance required (LDC § 25-8-42(B)(9)).
   111→- Pre-development watershed regs apply pre-diversion; only WQ treatment follows post-development receiving watershed (ECM 1.2.3).
   112→
   113→### Erosion Hazard Zone (DCM Appendix E)
   114→
   115→- EHZ analysis required when within 100 ft of a waterway centerline with DA ≥ 64 ac, or within 100–200 ft OHWM of the Colorado River below Longhorn Dam, or where significant erosion is present (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
   116→- **Exception:** site separated from triggering waterway by a public roadway (LDC § 25-7-32(B)).
   117→- Level 1 analysis projects 4H:1V slopes from future toe of bank (incision = existing depth × 3), min 20 ft setback from top of bank, max 100 ft in steep terrain.
   118→
   119→### EARZ / Void Mitigation (ECM 1.12)
   120→
   121→- EARZ sites require verbatim cover sheet note (ECM 1.12.3(A)(2)): trenching > 5 ft must be inspected by a Texas P.G. or representative.
   122→- Trenching/excavation in EARZ engages the Void and Water Flow Mitigation Rule and Std Spec 658S.
   123→
   124→### Plan set & standard details
   125→
   126→- SDP sheet size 24"×36" (DSD); AWU plans 22"×34" minimum (UCM 2.5.1.E.3).
   127→- PE seal required (preliminary seals not accepted; UCM 2.5.1.E.1).
   128→- Q1/Q2 IC tables (ECM App. Q) required in Suburban, Water Supply Rural/Suburban, and BSZ watersheds; **not** required in Urban watersheds (LDC § 25-8-62(F)).
   129→- Required standard details: 508S outlet structures, 661-1 (sed/filtration sand bed), 661-2 (wet pond clay liner — **prohibited over EARZ**), 661-3 (biofiltration), 662S-2 (pond maintenance road), DCM App. D Figs. 4-1 through 4-7 (inlets), 594S (gabion gradation), 414S (waterstops), 623S (dry-stack rock).
   130→
   131→### Construction / inspection
   132→
   133→- Pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282; waivable by Director).
   134→- Engineer of record certification before CO (General Site Plan Notes Construction Note 6).
   135→- **Pond perimeter signage** required only for residential or City-maintained SCMs; **exempt** if combined SCM storage ≤ 5,000 CF **AND** max ponding depth ≤ 3 ft (DCM 1.2.4.E.10).
   136→- BSZ commercial/MF water quality facilities require an **annual operating permit** (LDC § 25-8-233).
   137→- Subsurface commercial SCMs require **SPMP + annual PE inspection report** to WPD (LDC § 25-7-153(F); ECM 1.6.2.E).
   138→
   139→## Opportunities to evaluate
   140→
   141→- **RSMP payment in lieu of on-site detention** (DCM 8.2.2). Frees up developable area; current rate is on RSMP payment calculator. Eligibility depends on watershed (Feasibility Viewer) and order-of-preference justification. SMART Housing affordability stack yields 10–50% RSMP discount.
   142→- **DCM 1.2.2.G Simplified RSMP** for small sites (≤ 0.5 ac commercial/MF/mixed-use, or ≤ 1 ac SF subdivision) — skips three-scenario modeling.
   143→- **Fee-in-lieu of water quality controls** (LDC § 25-8-214(C); ECM 1.6.4; App. T) — **Urban Watersheds only**, with prior WPD Director approval. Unavailable in BSZ, Water Supply Suburban, and Water Supply Rural watersheds.
   144→- **Redevelopment Exception** to GSI / impervious cover increases:
   145→  - Urban/Suburban Redevelopment Exception (LDC § 25-8-25): no IC increase; unpermitted post-1992 development may be cured by removal.
   146→  - BSZ Redevelopment Exception (LDC § 25-8-26): commercial only; no pathway to cure unpermitted post-1992 development.
   147→- **Vested rights exemption from GSI/WQ** for development predating May 18, 1986 or previously permitted with WQ controls (ECM 1.9.2.A).
   148→- **Direct discharge to receiving water bodies** (Lady Bird, Austin, Travis, Colorado River, Waller TIRZ): no-increase standard does not apply (DCM 1.2.2.F).
   149→- **Shared SCMs / off-site treatment** — joint maintenance covenants (LDC § 25-7-153(C)) and UDAs let multiple lots share a single pond, reducing per-site footprint.
   150→- **Innovative stormwater practices** approved by the Director under LDC § 25-8-151 — non-standard SCMs with technical justification.
   151→- **Standard wall / SCM details from City Std Drawings** — using the published catalog (508S series, 661 series) avoids review back-and-forth on custom designs.
   152→
   153→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   154→
   155→- **`environmental.md`** — watershed classification (Urban / Suburban / BSZ / Water Supply Rural / Water Supply Suburban), EARZ status (in/out, NEARZ vs SEARZ), CEFs within 500 ft, water quality transition zone, IC limits by watershed, slope categories
   156→- **`floodplain.md` / `fwp` output** — FEMA + COA fully-developed 100-yr extents, regulatory floodplain, BFE, EHZ triggers, creek buffer
   157→- **`transportation.md`** — adjacent ROW geometry, ASMP classification, TxDOT vs city street, sidewalk widths, drive approach standards
   158→- **`wwp.md`** — adjacent utility easements (water/WW), required AW easement widths, conflicts with proposed grading
   159→- **`property-records.md`** — recorded easements (drainage, access, utility), restrictive covenants, prior RSMP Agreement, UDAs, plat notes
   160→- **`phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md`** — proposed IC, building footprint, parking, pond/SCM locations, grading extents, retaining wall heights and locations
   161→- **`programs/rsmp.md`** — eligibility flag and pathway determination
   162→- **`programs/smart-housing.md`** — if RSMP discount is being claimed
   163→
   164→## Output structure
   165→
   166→Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Findings list with severity, evidence, citation, and recommended action. Group by sub-topic where many findings overlap (drainage analysis, WQ controls, easements, walls, RSMP).
   167→
   168→## Severity heuristics
   169→
   170→| Finding | Severity |
   171→|---|---|
   172→| No viable drainage outfall — no downstream system within 300 ft and ROW cannot contain 100-yr fully developed flows | `significant` |
   173→| Site in COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain extending across proposed building/parking with no easement adjustment path | `significant` |
   174→| Dam-classified pond (≥ 6 ft embankment) required by site constraints without adequate clear zone | `significant` |
   175→| RSMP needed but project is a subdivision in Travis County ETJ (categorically ineligible) | `significant` |
   176→| EARZ site relying on clay liner (prohibited) — must redesign for geomembrane/concrete | `significant` if cost-prohibitive; otherwise `moderate` |
   177→| WQ control footprint + detention exceeds available pad area after setbacks/easements | `significant` |
   178→| Retaining wall > 10 ft supporting embankment without 20-ft maintenance zone | `moderate` |
   179→| Retaining wall ≥ 4 ft not flagged for separate building permit | `moderate` |
   180→| Wall proposed in drainage easement without Director approval pathway noted | `moderate` |
   181→| Interbasin diversion at/above threshold — variance required | `moderate` (timeline + Council exposure) |
   182→| Off-site SCM/shared pond proposed without joint maintenance covenant or UDA | `moderate` |
   183→| Subsurface commercial SCM proposed without SPMP + annual PE inspection commitment | `moderate` |
   184→| RSMP available and reduces on-site pond footprint | `opportunity` |
   185→| Fee-in-lieu of WQ available (Urban watershed) | `opportunity` |
   186→| SMART Housing stack yields RSMP payment discount | `opportunity` |
   187→| Urban/Suburban Redevelopment Exception preserves IC | `opportunity` |
   188→| Site discharges directly to Lady Bird/Lake Austin/Travis/Colorado River — no-increase rule waived | `opportunity` |
   189→| Standard configuration with adequate easements and downstream capacity | `note` |
   190→| Atlas 14 + COA fully-developed model needed but data available | `note` |
   191→
   192→## Common pitfalls
   193→
   194→- **Assuming RSMP waives the 2-year on-site storm control.** It doesn't (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8). Always require a separate 2-yr analysis.
   195→- **Assuming RSMP waives the 300-ft storm drain connection requirement** (DCM 1.2.3.C). Three narrow exceptions only.
   196→- **Citing the FEMA floodplain when COA fully-developed governs.** COA is typically broader; the drainage easement must extend to the COA WSE per DCM 1.2.4.F.
   197→- **Using clay liner over the EARZ.** Prohibited regardless of permeability (ECM 1.6.2.C). Don't list Std Detail 661-2 on EARZ plan sets.
   198→- **Treating "15 ft easement" as a minimum for enclosed pipes.** Not in current DCM 1.2.4.G — minimum is 20 ft.
   199→- **Same offsite IC assumption used in pond performance and spillway calcs.** Performance = existing IC; spillway = fully developed (DCM 8.3.2.A vs 8.3.3.A).
   200→- **Rain garden serving > 2 ac contributing area.** Must be designed as biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C/H) regardless of label.
   201→- **Counting only new IC in WQV.** WQV applies to 100% of IC, new + redeveloped (ECM 1.6.2.A).
   202→- **Trying to use RSMP for a Travis County ETJ subdivision.** Categorically unavailable.
   203→- **Trying to use WQ fee-in-lieu in the BSZ or Water Supply watersheds.** Urban Watersheds only.
   204→- **Assuming the BSZ Redevelopment Exception works for residential redevelopment.** Commercial only, and unpermitted post-1992 development cannot be cured.
   205→- **Underestimating retaining wall building-permit overhead.** Walls ≥ 4 ft trigger a separate IBC permit on a different review track.
   206→- **Universal "4 ft and accessible = safety rail" rule for retaining walls.** Not how TCM 13.2.10 works — function- and adjacent-use-driven.
   207→- **Missing the dam threshold at any point of perimeter.** A pond is a dam if any single point of the embankment reaches 6 ft (DCM 8.3.3.B.1); the whole facility is reclassified.
   208→- **Forgetting agency coordination for RSMP** — PARD parkland discharge, TxDOT ROW discharge, downstream jurisdiction approval can extend the schedule materially.
   209→- **Combining the existing and proposed drainage area maps on one sheet.** Must be separate sheets at the same scale for direct comparison.
   210→- **Citing superseded standards** — UBC (now IBC), "Watershed Engineering Division" (now "Office of the Director"), pre-Atlas 14 rainfall, BCM 15.4/15.10 for resubmittal/site plan requirements.
   211→- **Skipping the pre-Completeness-Check RSMP Feasibility Meeting.** A development cannot pass Completeness Check without it.

# Stormwater & Drainage Findings — 12713 Cinchring Ln

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 — Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision
**Proposed use:** Demolish existing SFR; build ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Lot area:** ~7,840 sq ft (0.18 acres), SF-2 zoning
**Watershed:** Walnut Creek — Suburban Watershed classification
**Floodplain:** Zone X (not in 100-year or 500-year floodplain)
**EARZ:** Not in Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone or Contributing Zone
**Date:** 2026-06-03

---

## Summary

- **Site Plan Lite drainage reforms exempt this lot from engineered drainage review and on-site detention.** At ~7,840 sq ft the lot is well under the 11,500 sq ft threshold; no drainage study, detention pond, or formal drainage plan is required, saving significant cost and schedule.
- **Impervious cover is capped at 45% (~3,528 sq ft) by the controlling SF-2 zoning limit**, which aligns with the Walnut Creek Suburban Watershed IC framework. The building footprint (40% / ~3,136 sq ft) plus driveways, sidewalks, and patios must stay within this envelope.
- **Water quality controls are likely satisfied by the existing Scofield subdivision regional facilities**, but this must be confirmed with the Watershed Protection Department since demolition-and-rebuild constitutes redevelopment subject to current WQ standards.
- **RSMP fee-in-lieu is a fallback option if detention is ever triggered**, but the Site Plan Lite exemption likely makes it unnecessary for this project. Eligibility in Walnut Creek watershed should be verified regardless.
- **No floodplain, EARZ, CEF, or erosion hazard zone constraints apply.** The site is in FEMA Zone X on upland terrain with no waterway within 100 ft, eliminating an entire class of drainage complications.

---

## Findings

### 1. Site Plan Lite Drainage Exemption

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | opportunity |
| **Citation** | Site Plan Lite Phase 2 (Ordinance adopted Mar 6, 2025, applications accepted Jun 16, 2025); LDC residential infill provisions |
| **Finding** | The Site Plan Lite drainage reforms exempt lots of 11,500 sq ft or less from drainage review. Lots up to 1 acre draining to an existing street or drainage system do not require on-site detention or an engineered drainage plan. This lot at ~7,840 sq ft qualifies on both counts. |
| **Implication** | The developer avoids the cost of an engineered drainage study, detention facility design, and associated review cycles. This removes what would otherwise be a $15,000-$40,000 engineering expense and 2-4 months of review time for a project of this scale. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm the lot drains to the existing street/storm system (expected for a platted Scofield lot on a local street). Verify with DSD that the exemption applies to demo-and-rebuild redevelopment, not just new construction on vacant lots. |

### 2. Impervious Cover Limit — 45%

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | moderate |
| **Citation** | LDC Sec. 25-2-492(D) (SF-2 site development regulations); LDC Sec. 25-8-392 (Suburban Watershed uplands IC); HOME Phase 1 Ordinance 20231207-001 |
| **Finding** | The SF-2 zoning impervious cover limit is 45%, yielding a maximum of ~3,528 sq ft of IC on this ~7,840 sq ft lot. The Walnut Creek Suburban Watershed IC limit for residential use is in the 45-50% range; the more restrictive of zoning or watershed controls. At 45%, the zoning limit is the binding constraint. Building coverage is separately capped at 40% (~3,136 sq ft). |
| **Implication** | After accounting for the building footprint (~3,136 sq ft maximum), only ~392 sq ft remains for driveways, sidewalks, patios, and other hardscape before hitting the IC ceiling. A two-story duplex with a smaller footprint would provide more IC headroom for site improvements. The developer must track IC carefully during design — exceeding 45% is a hard stop at permitting. |
| **Recommended next step** | Size the building footprint to leave adequate IC budget for driveways and walks. Consider pervious pavers or permeable materials for non-building hardscape to stay within the 45% limit. Cross-reference with the zoning/land-use (zlu) discipline for FAR and building coverage coordination. |

### 3. Water Quality — Redevelopment Compliance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | moderate |
| **Citation** | LDC Sec. 25-8-211; ECM Sec. 1.6.0; LDC Ch. 25-8 Subchapter A (Watershed Protection Ordinance — demolition/redevelopment) |
| **Finding** | Demolition of the existing SFR and construction of a new duplex constitutes redevelopment under Austin's Watershed Protection Ordinance. Redevelopment must comply with current water quality standards, including providing WQ controls for the developed impervious area. The WQ trigger threshold is 8,000 sq ft of new + redeveloped IC outside the BSZ. This lot's maximum IC (~3,528 sq ft) falls below the 8,000 sq ft trigger, which may exempt the project from on-site WQ controls entirely. |
| **Implication** | If the 8,000 sq ft WQ trigger is confirmed as not met, no structural water quality controls (rain garden, bioswale, sand filter) are required — a significant simplification. If WPD interprets the trigger differently for redevelopment (e.g., counting existing IC being replaced), the Scofield subdivision's existing regional WQ facilities may provide coverage, avoiding on-site treatment. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm with Watershed Protection Department (WPD) whether (a) the 8,000 sq ft IC threshold applies to this redevelopment, and (b) if triggered, whether existing Scofield regional facilities satisfy the WQ obligation for this lot. |

### 4. No On-Site Detention Required

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | DCM Sec. 1.2.2.D (no-increase rule); Site Plan Lite Phase 2 drainage reforms; DCM Sec. 1.2.2.G (Simplified RSMP for sites up to 1 acre) |
| **Finding** | Under the Site Plan Lite drainage reforms, lots up to 1 acre draining to an existing system are exempt from on-site detention requirements. This lot at 0.18 acres qualifies. Independently, the DCM Simplified RSMP pathway (Sec. 1.2.2.G) would also cover SF lots up to 1 acre if detention were otherwise triggered. The no-increase rule (2-, 10-, 25-, 100-year storms) does not apply when the exemption is in effect. |
| **Implication** | No detention pond, underground vault, or other flood-control structure is needed on site. This preserves the full buildable area for the duplex and site improvements. |
| **Recommended next step** | No action required beyond confirming the Site Plan Lite exemption applies (see Finding 1). |

### 5. RSMP Fee-in-Lieu Eligibility

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | opportunity |
| **Citation** | DCM Sec. 8.2; DCM Sec. 1.2.2.G (Simplified RSMP); RSMP Participation Handbook |
| **Finding** | The RSMP allows qualifying developments to pay a fee-in-lieu of constructing on-site detention. For SF lots up to 1 acre, the Simplified RSMP pathway (DCM 1.2.2.G) applies — no three-scenario HEC-HMS modeling required. Walnut Creek is within COA full-purpose jurisdiction and is expected to be an eligible watershed, but this must be confirmed via the RSMP Feasibility Viewer. |
| **Implication** | RSMP is likely unnecessary given the Site Plan Lite detention exemption. However, if project scope changes (e.g., lot subdivision, additional units beyond duplex) push the project past the exemption threshold, RSMP provides a viable fallback. The RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before any formal Completeness Check — a sequencing requirement to keep in mind. |
| **Recommended next step** | Verify Walnut Creek watershed eligibility on the RSMP Feasibility Viewer (austintexas.gov/RSMP). No action needed now unless the project scope changes. |

### 6. Floodplain — No Constraint

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | FEMA FIRM Panel 48453C0115E (effective 06/16/1993); property survey; LDC Sec. 25-7-92 |
| **Finding** | The property is in FEMA Zone X — outside the 100-year and 500-year floodplain. The site sits at approximately 850-870 ft elevation, well above the Walnut Creek floodplain corridor. No COA fully-developed 100-year floodplain encroachment is expected given the upland location. No floodplain development permit, CLOMR/LOMR, or elevation certificate is required. |
| **Implication** | No floodplain-related restrictions on building placement, grading, or finished floor elevation. Cross-referenced with the floodplain (fwp) discipline — confirmed Zone X, no creek buffer applies. |
| **Recommended next step** | None. |

### 7. EARZ and CEF — No Constraint

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | TCEQ Edwards Aquifer Protection Program, 30 TAC Ch. 213; LDC Sec. 25-8-281 et seq.; ECM Sec. 1.10.0; ECM Sec. 1.12 |
| **Finding** | The property is not within the Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone or Contributing Zone. No TCEQ Edwards Aquifer Protection Plan (EAPP) is required. No known Critical Environmental Features (caves, sinkholes, springs, rimrock) exist at or adjacent to the site. The EARZ-specific prohibitions (clay liner prohibition, void mitigation, geomembrane requirements) do not apply. |
| **Implication** | No EARZ-related design constraints, liner requirements, or void mitigation protocols. No CEF buffers (150-300 ft) restrict the buildable area. |
| **Recommended next step** | CEF status will be formally confirmed via the Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) form required at permitting. No early action needed. |

### 8. Erosion Hazard Zone — Not Triggered

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | DCM Appendix E; LDC Sec. 25-7-32 |
| **Finding** | EHZ analysis is required when a site is within 100 ft of a waterway centerline with a drainage area of 64 acres or more. The Scofield subdivision is an upland residential area with no major waterway within 100 ft of this lot. No EHZ analysis is required. |
| **Implication** | No erosion setback restricts the buildable area. |
| **Recommended next step** | None. |

### 9. Storm Drain Connection — Verify Proximity

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | data-gap |
| **Citation** | DCM Sec. 1.2.3.C (as amended 9-8-2025) |
| **Finding** | A storm drain connection is required when a site is within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system. Scofield is a fully developed subdivision with curb-and-gutter streets that likely include storm drain infrastructure. The Site Plan Lite exemption from drainage review may moot this requirement for a duplex, but the underlying obligation to connect to (and not adversely affect) existing infrastructure remains. |
| **Implication** | If the lot drains to the street and the street drains to a functioning storm system, the requirement is satisfied by default. If the lot has rear-yard drainage that does not reach the street, site grading must ensure positive drainage to the public system. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm during design that the finished grade directs all runoff to Cinchring Ln and the existing curb/inlet system. No formal storm drain design is expected to be required. |

### 10. S.M.A.R.T. Housing RSMP Discount

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | opportunity |
| **Citation** | RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24); S.M.A.R.T. Housing Policy |
| **Finding** | If RSMP participation is pursued, a 10-50% payment discount is available for projects with S.M.A.R.T. Housing certification (10-50% affordable units maintained for 40+ years). For a 2-unit duplex, this would require dedicating 1 unit as income-restricted. |
| **Implication** | Only relevant if (a) RSMP participation becomes necessary and (b) the developer is pursuing an affordability-linked project. At this scale, the RSMP fee itself is modest, so the discount may not justify the 40-year affordability commitment. |
| **Recommended next step** | Evaluate only if project scope changes to trigger detention requirements and the developer is interested in affordability programs. |

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Site Plan Lite applicability to demo-and-rebuild redevelopment.** Does the drainage review exemption (lots <=11,500 sq ft) apply to demolition-and-new-construction on an existing platted lot, or only to greenfield construction? Confirm with DSD before relying on the exemption.

2. **WQ trigger for this IC level.** The site's maximum IC (~3,528 sq ft) is below the 8,000 sq ft WQ trigger threshold. Confirm with WPD that this threshold applies to redevelopment IC (replaced + new) and that the project is exempt from structural water quality controls.

3. **Scofield regional WQ facilities.** If WQ controls are triggered, do existing regional stormwater facilities serving the Scofield subdivision satisfy the water quality obligation for this lot? The subdivision was developed in the late 1980s/early 1990s and may have regional ponds. WPD confirmation is needed.

4. **Existing drainage pattern.** Does the lot currently drain entirely to Cinchring Ln (front), or does any portion drain to the rear or side toward adjacent lots? Positive drainage to the street is assumed but should be confirmed by a topographic survey or site visit before design.

5. **RSMP watershed eligibility.** Is Walnut Creek confirmed as a participating RSMP watershed on the Feasibility Viewer? This is a contingency question — only matters if the project scope changes beyond the Site Plan Lite exemption threshold.

6. **IC accounting method.** For the 45% IC limit, does WPD use gross lot area (~7,840 sq ft) or net site area (excluding easements/ROW dedications) as the denominator? The 5-ft PUE along the lot line and any ROW dedication could reduce the effective denominator and tighten the IC budget.

7. **Interbasin diversion.** Confirm that the lot drains entirely within the Walnut Creek watershed and that no grading changes would divert runoff across a watershed boundary (unlikely given the suburban setting, but required for due diligence under LDC Sec. 25-8-365).
